messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran long-context load tests on Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private and hit sustained KV cache growth on Dedicated for sequences > 65k tokens. Memory climbs steadily until OOM unless we evict aggressively. Repro steps + small profiles below.

leo: Oof. Did you see fragmentation or just overall RSS growth?

maya: Both. RSS up ~18% over 30m on a steady chat replay. smaps shows a lot of anon pages with 'AnonHugePages' toggling, and frequent page faults in the runtime when GC/evict kicks in. Fragmentation correlates with many small allocations from KV pages.

sam: Is this only Dedicated? Any config diff from Hosted/Private kernels or jemalloc settings?

maya: Configs mostly aligned but Dedicated nodes use kernel 6.1 and host uses 5.15 family (cloud image). Dedicated has THP disabled, different hugetlb fallback, and we ship jemalloc 5.3 on Dedicated vs 5.2 on Hosted (due to packaging).

nina: Could be allocation pathways + kernel mm heuristics interacting. Did you capture pprof/heap profiles and a perf top?

maya: Yep. Attached snippets (paste):

```
# pmap -x <pid>
Address           Kbytes     RSS   Dirty Mode  Mapping
000055b8e7600000  1310720  948000  948000 rw---  runtime_kv_pages
...
# /proc/<pid>/smaps (excerpt)
AnonHugePages:  786432 kB
Rss:           948000 kB
Referenced:    943200 kB
KernelPageSize:  4096 kB
MMUPageSize:    2097152 kB
```

maya: perf shows hot paths in kv_page_alloc() + evict_scan(), and a surprising number of minor page faults when reading cold KV frames under Dedicated.

leo: Minor page faults with big hugepage counts suggests our mmap/munmap + madvise pattern isn't matching kernel expectations. If Dedicated kernel's madvise behavior differs, we could get pages not reclaimed and fragmented arenas.

ops-bot: @channel Notice: repro cluster (dedicated-prod-test-4) reserved until 20:30 UTC for debugging.

sam: Two quick theories: (1) jemalloc version/opt flags cause different slab packing causing small free extents -> fragmentation under long-run allocations; (2) kernel hugetlb/hugepage fallback leads to mixed page sizes, which fragments the KV arena and prevents contiguous reclaiming. Both lead to steady RSS even after evict.

nina: Also check network MTU/VPC path: we saw earlier that VPC segmentation sometimes causes long tail in receive path, increasing outstanding requests and temporarily pinning KV frames in-flight, blocking eviction. Did you compare request concurrency/queue lengths?

maya: Yes — Dedicated tests had higher in-flight concurrency (we stress with burst policy). When we rerun with stricter batching heuristics (max-inflight 64 -> 24) the memory growth slows but doesn't disappear. So batching helps but it's not sole cause.

leo: Good signal. Can you capture a kernel-level page-report: /proc/vmstat and slabinfo around the spike? Also want thread stacks from perf on the evict stall.

maya: Posted excerpts:
```
# /proc/vmstat (delta over 5m)
pgpgin  1234567
pgpgout  543210
pswpin  0
pswpout 0
nr_hugepages 0
nr_free_pages  12000
nr_inactive_anon  60000
nr_active_anon  40000
```

# slabinfo (top lines)
slab_unreclaimable  23456
kmalloc-2048         12000
```

sam: No swp, so kernel can't offload. If Dedicated has stricter memcg limits or different oom_kill behavior, that aligns. Also slab_unreclaimable high indicates fragmentation at kernel allocator level.

leo: Action items I propose:
- reproduce on a small Dedicated node with minimal extras and collect: pmap, smaps, pprof heap, perf top, /proc/vmstat, slabinfo, and a 60s perf record around heavy evict round.
- run against Hosted and Private with same synthetic load and identical jemalloc build to narrow runtime vs kernel.
- try toggling MADV_DONTNEED vs MADV_FREE in evict path and measure page reclaim.

nina: Add to that: capture network queue stats (ethtool -S) and NIC driver ring drops, and check PCIe BAR mapping differences on on-prem GPUs. On-prem had a different BAR size that affected DMA scatter/gather in past.

maya: I implemented a quick patch switching to MADV_FREE for kernels >= 5.8 and ran smoke test — memory plateaued lower for Dedicated (roughly -12% peak). Not a full fix but promising. Patch gist: 
```
if (kernel_supports_madv_free()) {
  madvise(addr, len, MADV_FREE);
} else {
  madvise(addr, len, MADV_DONTNEED);
}
```

leo: Nice. That aligns with kernel behavior differences. Let's be careful: MADV_FREE is lazy and may keep pages until pressure, but it avoids immediate faults. Could reduce fault storm. We should benchmark latency tail.

maya: Latency P95 stayed within SLO; P99 improved slightly. CPU for evict thread dropped ~18%.

sam: Next: create a minimal reproducer that allocates many intermediate KV frames then random access to force fragmentation. We'll run it across environments. Also try rebuilding jemalloc w/ opt to reduce fragmentation (experiment: opt.background_thread=false, lg_bin)

nina: I'll coordinate infra to spin identical kernels across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for at least one run. Also will check if VPC MTU mismatches/encapsulation (GRO/TSO) are creating reassembly latency that pins frames.

ops-bot: @maya @leo Next steps created: ISSUE-INT-482 assigned to maya, priority P1, due 48h. Logs attached to issue.

maya: OK I'm pushing the MADV_FREE branch to a feature flag in canary and running a long-run with identical concurrency. Will post profiles in the issue. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

leo: Good work. If MADV_FREE keeps helping we'll roll it behind a runtime flag and add kernel-doc tests. Also add a jemalloc variant to our perf matrix.

sam: One more note: if we still see fragmentation after this, consider compressing old KV frames into a compact store (compact-on-evict) to reduce allocator pressure. Might be useful for on-prem with limited memory.

maya: Agreed. For now MADV_FREE + conservative batching reduced the steady growth enough to avoid immediate OOM. We'll iterate.

infra-bot: repro cluster ded-prod-test-4 snapshot uploaded to /mnt/debug-snapshots/1802504763.tar.gz

maya: I'll follow up with the issue update when long-run finishes. Thanks everyone.
